title: MoDr: Mixture-of-Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Test-Time Reasoning
claim: A single fixed recurrent path limits reasoning; routing each step among multiple specialized branches enables adaptive, dynamic exploration.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels split by dashed line, with branch zoom-in inset
description: Two panels separated by a vertical dashed line. Panel (a), 'Depth-Recurrent Huginn Model', shows a static reasoning process. Question tokens enter at the bottom. A gray block holds a yellow Prelude (P), a chain of identical pink Recurrent (R) blocks starting from noise S0, and a maroon Coda (C). Dashed 'e' arrows inject the input embedding. Pale pink step boxes along the top feed into an 'Answer' dashed box. Panel (b), 'Mixture-of-Depth-Recurrent Transformer (Ours)', has the same layout, but the R chain is replaced by a Router plus a rainbow-gradient Multi-Branch Recurrent Module. Reasoning step boxes are multicolored. A zoomed inset on the right shows branches 1, 2 and N, with ✗ marks on the unselected branches and ✓ on the chosen one. A legend at the bottom explains the symbols. The eye goes first to the colorful router and branch inset.
caption: Comparison of (a) vanilla Huginn (Geiping et al., 2025) model and (b) MoDr (ours) reasoning patterns. Unlike Huginn, where each reasoning step relies on a single recurrent module, our proposed MoDr employs a dynamic routing mechanism to adaptively select the most suitable recurrent branch for the current context input, thereby predicting the next token. During inference, in Huginn, each token is generated by a fixed recurrent module, whereas in MoDr, tokens are produced dynamically through a sequential relay of multiple recurrent branches.
abstract: Large Language Models have demonstrated superior reasoning capabilities by generating step-by-step reasoning in natural language before deriving the final answer. Recently, Geiping et al. introduced 3.5B-Huginn as an alternative to this paradigm, a depth-recurrent Transformer that increases computational depth per token by reusing a recurrent block in latent space. Despite its performance gains with increasing recurrences, this approach is inadequate for tasks demanding exploration and adaptivity, a limitation arising from its single, chain-like propagation mechanism. To address this, we propose a novel dynamic multi-branches routing approach for Huginn, termed as Mixture-of-Depth-Recurrent (MoDr) Transformer, which enables effective exploration of the solution space by shifting linear latent reasoning into a LoRA-based multi-branch dynamic relay mode with a learnable hard-gate routing. Meanwhile, we introduce an auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy to mitigate the potential routing collapse. Our empirical results reveal that MoDr achieves average accuracy improvements of +7.2% and +2.48% over the original Huginn model and its fine-tuned variant, respectively, across various mathematical reasoning benchmarks and improvements of +21.21% and +1.52% on commonsense reasoning benchmarks.
